title: Room-by-Room Holiday Hosting Checklist | Hippo
summary: Home repairs can feel intimidating, but they don't have to be. These five tasks can be done in less than a day and will help prevent more serious repairs later.
body_markdown:
The best holiday gatherings look effortless. A little prep behind the scenes is why.


It’s not a coincidence that hosting season and home fire safety season overlap. According to the[National Fire Protection Association](https://www.nfpa.org/about-nfpa/press-room/news-releases/2025/december-among-leading-months-of-the-year-for-us-home-fires) , Thanksgiving is the leading day of the year for home cooking fires, with Christmas Eve and Christmas Day close behind. More cooking, more candles, and more people in the house all add up.


> “A few extra minutes of prep go further during hosting season than almost any other time of year,” said Courtney Klosterman, home insights expert at Hippo. “The hosts who feel most at ease are usually the ones who’ve already handled the small stuff.”


Work through this room-by-room checklist before opening your doors, so you can focus on what matters, your guests.


## Greet guests with a warm welcome


Good lighting and clear paths set the tone before anyone even rings the doorbell.


- Light the path from your driveway or walkway to your front door, adding a porch or path light where it’s dark
- Switch on a few interior entry lamps so guests aren’t stepping from dark to bright
- Shovel first, then salt with a thin, even layer, especially on steps and where guests exit their cars
- Set out mats for wet shoes and umbrellas
- Clear a closet, basket, or bench for coats and bags


## A living room ready for mingling


After guests settle in, your living room usually sees the most activity. A few easy adjustments create good flow.


### Seating flow


- Remove the coffee table or recliner that takes up too much space
- Group chairs in small clusters so people can chat without blocking others
- Create clear paths between the entry, the food and drinks, and the seating


### Rugs, cords, and walkways


- Tape down the edges of area rugs or add a non-slip pad underneath
- Reroute extension cords along walls, or cover them with a cord cover
- Store any fragile items in walkways you don’t want accidentally knocked over


### Candles, trees, and decor


- Place real candles on stable, flat surfaces away from curtains, greenery, and anything flammable, or swap in flameless candles instead
- If you have a real tree, water it every day and keep it away from fireplaces, radiators, and space heaters
- Check string lights for frayed edges or broken sockets, and unplug them when things wind down


## A kitchen for cooking and gathering


The kitchen is the heart of the party. It’s common for guests to congregate around an island or bartop for conversation while food is being prepped. A few checks keep it running smoothly.


- Clear the stovetop and surrounding area of dish towels, paper products, and anything flammable
- Keep pot handles turned inward and keep an eye on active burners
- Sharpen dull knives and store them in a block or on a magnetic strip, not loose in a drawer
- Test your blender, mixer, and food processor, checking cords and lids beforehand
- Press the test button on your smoke detector and swap in fresh batteries if it chirps
- Place a fire extinguisher somewhere easy to reach, like under the sink or near the kitchen exit, and check that the gauge is in the green
- Know where your water shutoff valve is, usually near the water meter, in the basement, utility room, garage, or on an exterior wall, and make sure anyone helping out knows too


## A thoughtful bathroom says a lot


Guests notice the little things, especially when you’ve thought of what they might need for their holiday visit.


- Clear a counter or flat surface for phones and purses
- Lay a non-slip mat by the sink or tub
- Set out liquid hand soap, a clean hand towel, air freshener, and a small trash bin
- Stock extra toilet paper within easy reach
- Make sure the bathroom and hallway leading to it are clear and well lit


## One last thing


Before your first guest rings the bell, confirm your homeowners coverage and limits are where you want them, in case there’s a mishap. The prep work is done. Now it’s just you, your guests, and the holiday cheer.
